Appearance:
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Government Advocate for appellant/State.
Judgment
ON BOARD Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal

This appeal is filed by the State being aggrieved of judgment dated 07/08/2015 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Anuppur in Special Case No.04/2015, whereby learned trial Court has acquitted the accused Rohit Mishra, aged about 19 years from charges under Sections 363, 366, 342 and 376(1) of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act.

2. It is submitted that as per school records, victim was a minor at the time of the incident,
therefore, acquittal could not have been recorded merely on the basis of FSL report being negative.
It is submitted that in a rural setup there are several circumstances which prevents a woman from lodging report in time.
But there is no reason to disbelieve the story of victim and record a finding of acquittal contrary to the material available on record.
Thus, Shri Manas Mani Verma, Government Advocate submits that finding of acquittal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9254 2 CRA-1569-2016 be reversed and appeal be allowed.

3. It is submitted that vide (Ex.P/13) 10th marksheet was seized and that is Article 'A', in which date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 20/08/1998, whereas incident is of 26/02/2015, therefore,
victim being a minor, finding of acquittal be reversed and conviction be recorded.
4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record.

sentences.text: It is evident that prosecution story in short is that on 26/02/2015, victim (PW/1) lodged a report in writing at Police Station Jaithari that (PW/1) aged about 16 years has been lured by accused Rohit Mishra and Rajendra Rathore.
She was seen in the company of these two accused persons being taken on a motorcycle by Mandhari Kol.

6. On the basis of said written report, case crime No.35/2015 was registered against Rohit Mishra under Sections 363, 34 of IPC.
7.

During investigation, victim was recovered on 26/02/2015 from the house of Chintamani Tiwari,
where Gaytari Rathore was residing as tenant.
Recovery panchnama is Ex.P/1 and thereafter, victim was sent for medical examination.

After taking consent of the father of the victim, she was forwarded to the District Hospital, Annupur, where victim had refused to undergo medical examination, where again she was sent to District Hospital, Annupur on 01/03/2015 where Dr. Alka Tiwari had carried out medical examination and had seized underwear as well as vaginal swab and had prepared two slides and handed over to woman constable Lekhanwati.

8. On hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:9254 3 CRA-1569-2016 record, it is evident that lady Doctor (PW/9) Dr. Alka Tiwari had adviced X- Ray to determine the age.

Dr. Tiwari noted that victim was fully conscious,
her pulse and BP was normal, gait was normal.
There were no external injury marks on her body.
In internal examination, Doctor had found that there were no injury marks.
Her hymen was old torn and broken.
Dr. further stated that on examining the X-Ray, she found that her ulna and radius bones was fully fused and had determined the age of the victim to be between 17-19 years.
9. Victim in her 164 statement Ex.P/2 has stated that no untoward incident had taken place with her.

She categorically stated that though she has gone with Rohit Mishra as she was upset with her family members on 26/5/2015 but Rohit had kept her in the house of his brother-in-law and had not done anything wrong to her.
Prior to that he had taken her for a picnic on 01/11/2014 where too, no wrong was performed on her.
10. (PW/6) father of the victim in para 8 of his cross-examination has admitted that his marriage was performed as a child marriage.
It was performed at such a tender age that he does not remember the date.
His gauna was performed when he was 13 years of age.

After one year of gauna,
prosecutrix was born.
Therefore, prosecutrix was a consenting adult.
There is no other material on record to dispute the evidence of her father or that of the ossification test report.

11. School teacher (PW/20) Shri Krishna Pal Rathore though stated that date of birth of victim is mentioned as 20/08/1998 in the record and she had taken admission on 10/07/2004 in Class 1 but in cross-examination NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9254 4 CRA-1569-2016 admits that admission form Ex.P/38 was not seized.
He admits that on Ex.P/39 there is over writing and whitener was used to correct the date of birth of the victim.

Even there is whitener on the name of the victim and therefore, when these facts are taken on consideration then ossification report clearly points out that victim was an adult, a fact which is corroborated through the evidence of her father coupled with the facts that there are manipulations in the school record, date of birth could not be The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Rohit Mishra on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50242623/
2 proved otherwise while the prosecution, when tested, the impugned judgment of acquittal holding that consensual relationship between two adults is not an offence and cannot be faulted under the facts and circumstances calling for interference.

sentences.text:
Interference with the order of acquittal is called for only in exceptional cases - where there is manifest error of law of procedure resulting into miscarriage of justice,
and, where the acquittal has been caused by shutting out evidence which otherwise ought to have been considered or where material evidence which clinches the issue has been overlooked.
In such exceptional cases, the High Court can set aside an order of acquittal, but it cannot covert it into one of conviction.
The only course left to the High Court in such exception cases, is to order retrial."

13. When the law on the subject is taken into consideration then NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:9254 5 CRA-1569-2016

admittedly we find no illegality in the impugned judgment judgment dated 07.08.2015 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Anuppur in Special Case No.04/2015, acquitting the accused persons from the charges under Sections 363, 366, 342 and 376(1) of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act.
14. Accordingly, this appeal fails and is dismissed.
15. Let record of the Trial Court be sent back forthwith.
